html:
A Black religious and political movement founded in Detroit in 1930 by Wallace Fard Muhammad. It uses the language of Islam, but its teachings differ greatly from mainstream Islam.

After Fard disappeared in 1934, Elijah Muhammad led it for four decades. He taught that Black people were the original people and should build their own nation apart from white America. The movement ran businesses, schools and farms, and stressed discipline, clean living and self-reliance. It drew many followers in the cities of the North, swollen by the Great Migration, and in prisons.

Its most famous minister was Malcolm X, who spread its message in the 1950s and early 1960s. He broke with it in 1964, turned to Sunni Islam, and was murdered in 1965 by members of the Nation. The boxer Muhammad Ali also joined. After Elijah Muhammad died in 1975, his son Warith Deen Mohammed led most followers into mainstream Sunni Islam. Louis Farrakhan rebuilt the Nation on the old teachings in the late 1970s.
sum: A Black religious and political movement founded in Detroit in 1930 by Wallace Fard Muhammad. It uses the language of Islam, but its teachings differ greatly from mainstream Islam.
